persistence_invariants.brief: A composite unique constraint on (sku, location) guarantees at most one stored record per pair; a repeat write collapses to that row rather than duplicating.
quantity, sku, location, and inventory_code are NOT NULL so a filed record always carries its addressing key and stored values.
A CHECK (quantity >= 0) constraint enforces that stock never persists below zero (R2 write-time rejection backed at the DB).
The read-existing-then-write for a (sku, location) collision runs in a single transaction so a concurrent repeat file cannot store two rows.

nfrs.brief: Existing stock data survives every additive schema migration with no loss; each inventory adjustment keeps an unmodifiable timestamp and actor.
nfrs.fitness_function: Real-branch migration test: seed records, apply the next additive migration, assert prior records intact and timestamp/actor immutable.

nfrs.brief: Stock levels never go below zero and never overcommit; an overcommitting pick is rejected at write time (no stored negative, no double-allocation).
nfrs.fitness_function: Service-layer + DB CHECK (PI3) test on the real branch: attempt an overcommitting write and assert rejection with no negative row stored.

nfrs.brief: Every (sku, location) is uniquely addressable; a collision is resolved at write time (no duplicate stored, no error page).
nfrs.fitness_function: Real-branch integration test (AC3): file twice for the same pair, assert exactly one row and updated values; DB unique constraint PI1 enforces it.

nfrs.brief: Integration tests run against the paired Lakebase branch, never a mock or in-memory substitute; CI refuses to merge a PR whose integration tests do not run against a real branch.
nfrs.fitness_function: pytest-bdd suite bound to DATABASE_URL of the paired branch with Alembic applied first; CI gate asserts no in-memory/mocked DB driver.

nfrs.brief: The UI is a React + TypeScript single-page application under client/ that navigates client-side with no full-page reloads; the backend boundary returns JSON, not server-rendered HTML.
nfrs.fitness_function: Boundary layer declared renders_via: react (JSON only); client ships its own component tests; fitness check asserts no server-side template rendering in app/routes.

nfrs.brief: Validation messages name the offending field rather than a generic 'bad request' (PO preference), owned at the API boundary.
nfrs.fitness_function: Boundary validation test asserts the error payload identifies the specific invalid field.

nfrs.brief: Config in env (twelve-factor): the app connects to databricks_postgres via the DATABASE_URL written by the post-checkout hook; the database name is not renamed or made app-specific.
nfrs.fitness_function: Config-in-env fitness check: no hardcoded connection string; DATABASE_URL sourced from env and points at the paired branch's databricks_postgres.
